purpose: This medication is used to treat bacterial infections such as ear infections, sinus infections, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and skin infections. It works against bacteria that may be resistant to amoxicillin alone. Your doctor prescribed it because the bacteria causing your infection are best treated with this combination.
how_it_works: Amoxicillin is an antibiotic that kills bacteria by breaking down their protective outer wall. Some sneaky bacteria produce an enzyme called beta-lactamase that can destroy amoxicillin before it works. Clavulanate is added to block that enzyme, so the amoxicillin can do its job and wipe out the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and stomach upset. You may also notice a skin rash in some cases. Taking this medication with food can help reduce stomach upset and diarrhea.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics, as you could have a serious allergic reaction. Stop taking it and seek help right away if you develop hives, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Let your doctor know if you have liver or kidney problems before taking this medication. Also, finishing the entire course of antibiotics is very important, even if you feel better early, to make sure the infection is fully cleared.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet every 8 to 12 hours, depending on the strength your doctor prescribed. It is best taken at the start of a meal to reduce stomach upset. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions, and take every dose as directed until the prescription is finished.
